To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

29% of breast cancer patients with DCIS or early stage invasive disease reported moderate-to-high fear of cancer recurrence at 2 years post-diagnosis, which may be reduced by management of anxiety, provision for social support, and education.

fear of cancer recurrence (defined as moderate-to-high levels) at 2-years after treatment was reported by 29% of breast cancer patients, was associated with younger age, higher stage, lower social support, higher anxiety, and was higher in women with early invasive breast cancer compared with those with DCIS.
fear of cancer recurrence (a common and persistent concern) is associated with young age, stage IIB breast cancer, and lower social support and anxiety.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fear of cancer recurrence (hereafter FCR) in women who have had breast cancer.
the fear of cancer recurrence (hereinafter, FCR) in women with breast cancer.
the development of a new approach to the development of a cancer recurrence in the context of a cancer recurrence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FCR is a significant concern among DCIS survivors and EIBC survivors.
FCR was low in most DCIS patients, but moderate-to-high FCR was common among younger patients with stage IIA disease and those with elevated anxiety or poor social support.
FCR is a common and potentially distressful experience for women with DCIS and EICB, and that it is a multidimensional experience.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

fear of cancer recurrence (i.e., concern about recurrence) is common in women with duct carcinoma in situ (i.e., DCIS) or early breast cancer (EBC) and may be associated with anxiety and social support.
fear of recurrence is a common concern among breast cancer patients, and that it may be particularly high among younger women, and among those with early-stage disease, especially stage IIa disease.
younger age, higher stage at diagnosis, and lower social support are independently associated with higher levels of fear of recurrence in breast cancer survivors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FCR is common in DCIS and early invasive breast cancers, and that it is associated with younger age, higher stage, and lower social support.
fear of recurrence is common in women with DCIS and EIBCs, but it is not a significant problem in the vast majority of patients.
fear of cancer recurrence is not uncommon among breast cancer survivors, even those with ductal carcinoma insitu (DCIS) who are at low risk for recurrence.
